headline: RBI issues final KYC Amendment Directions on suspected money mule accounts
summary_points: RBI has issued final KYC Amendment Directions for a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) on suspected money mule accounts and cyber-enabled frauds.
The SOP sets a uniform, time-bound procedure for banks to suo moto place temporary debit holds on suspected amounts or accounts.
Holds are to be removed in coordination with Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs), while protecting genuine customers from inconvenience.
The draft of 11 September 2026 was revised after stakeholder feedback; a statement on feedback is in the Annex.
Effective 1 July 2027, or any earlier date a bank chooses to implement the SOP.
who_is_affected: Commercial banks, small finance banks, payments banks, local area banks, regional rural banks and urban co-operative banks, and their customers.
action_required: Banks should review the final Directions, update KYC and fraud-handling processes and systems, and be ready to implement the SOP by 1 July 2027 or earlier.

social.linkedin:
RBI has issued final Amendment Directions on 'Suspected Money Mule Accounts to Prevent Cyber-enabled Financial Frauds' (Press Release 2026-2027/1584, dated 27 November 2026).

The Directions lay down a Standard Operating Procedure giving banks a uniform, time-bound process to suo moto place temporary debit holds on amounts or accounts suspected to be linked to money mule activity and cyber-enabled frauds. Holds are to be removed in coordination with Law Enforcement Agencies, with safeguards to protect genuine customers from inconvenience.

Key points:
- Draft issued on 11 September 2026; revised after stakeholder feedback
- Separate KYC Amendment Directions for commercial banks, SFBs, payments banks, LABs, RRBs and UCBs
- Effective 1 July 2027, or earlier if a bank decides to implement the SOP

Finance, compliance and risk teams in banks should start mapping their processes now.

Please verify the details with the official RBI source before acting.
